unit: Convex foundations and scope correction to SGPT Part I
files_read: New convex history section and affected historical transitions; complete retained source convex appendix previously read. Earlier P01 regularity and Q01 mixed-discriminant inputs consulted at their verified scope.
source_locators_checked: SGPT root lines 204–209 and complete Part I/II/III openings: exact five-chapter Part I boundary.
Complete 740-line SGPT convex appendix; source delegated statements distinguished from already proved results and broader unproved scopes.

Hörmander 2007 reprint: complete Theorem 2.1.10 and Corollaries 2.1.11–2.1.13 pp. 44–45; Theorem 2.1.22 pp. 55–56; Propositions 2.2.1–2.2.2, Definition 2.2.3 and Theorem 2.2.4 pp. 66–68; Theorem 2.2.5 pp. 68–69; Theorem 2.2.8 p. 70. proof_scope: Finite-dimensional separation, local convex regularity and almost-everywhere differentiability; proper closed Fenchel duality; finite-primal attained sum duality; bounded slope growth and decreasing smooth approximation; completed-measurable subgradient pushforward and Radon construction; vague continuity, tightness distinction, C1,1 Hessian formula and positive mixed-measure polarization. Lower-dimensional reference bodies and dimension zero treated explicitly. General relative-domain attained sum duality remains outside this unit.
review_method: Scoped authoring-agent mathematical/editorial review, not independent certification. All seven contact sheets of 26 selected integrated PDF pages inspected before the second complete direct chapter read. After a source EOF whitespace correction, all 26 final selected rendered page images are pixel-identical to the inspected first version; that image comparison carries forward their visual inspection. PDF metadata bytes differ. Zero audit errors, unresolved references/citations, overfull or underfull boxes.
remaining_obligations: Ample toric elementary geometry and lattice counting; complete five-chapter Part I proof-gap/overlap audit.
Earlier internal FN, global mass/bigness, full envelope contact and relative equation uniqueness/bounds interfaces; integration and two whole-prequel reads.
